title: Watch the light hit El Capitan in Yosemite Valley
description: Granite walls a kilometre high above a glacial valley. US national parks restrict dogs to paved areas and campgrounds only.

title: Climb the cables up Half Dome
description: 24km return with 1,460m of climb, finishing on two steel cables up bare granite. Permits are by lottery and people have died on the cables.

title: Catch the Horsetail Fall firefall in February
description: For about two weeks the setting sun lights a thin fall on El Capitan so it glows like molten rock. Needs water in the fall and a cloudless west horizon.

title: Stand under General Sherman in Sequoia National Park
description: The largest tree on earth by volume - 1,487 cubic metres, and still adding the equivalent of a mature tree's worth of wood every year.

title: Climb Mount Whitney, the highest point in the lower 48
description: 4,421m via 35km and 1,900m of ascent, usually done in one brutal day. Day-use permits are a February lottery.

title: Find the movie locations in the Alabama Hills
description: Rounded granite used in more than 400 films, with Mobius Arch framing Whitney behind it. BLM land, so dogs and free camping are both fine.

title: Walk among the tufa towers at Mono Lake
description: Calcium spires exposed when Los Angeles diverted the inflow streams and the lake dropped 14m. A court case in 1994 stopped it going dry.

title: Walk the streets of Bodie ghost town
description: A gold town of 10,000 abandoned to arrested decay - about 100 buildings left standing exactly as found, with goods still on the shop shelves.

title: Watch sunrise over the dunes in Death Valley
description: The hottest place ever reliably recorded at 56.7C, and the lowest in North America at 86m below sea level. Do not come in July.

title: Find the moving rocks at Racetrack Playa
description: Stones that leave trails across the dry lake, finally explained in 2014 as thin ice floating them along. 43km of tyre-shredding washboard to reach.

title: Sleep under the Joshua trees
description: Where the Mojave meets the Colorado desert, with monzogranite boulders, a Dark Sky Park designation and rock climbing everywhere you look.

title: Climb Salvation Mountain
description: Leonard Knight spent nearly thirty years building a hill out of adobe and half a million litres of donated paint, beside the shrinking Salton Sea.

title: Drive Highway 1 through Big Sur
description: 140km of coast road on the edge of the Santa Lucia range. Landslides close sections for months at a time - check before committing.

title: Walk the headlands at Point Lobos
description: Called the greatest meeting of land and water in the world by the painter Francis McComas - sea otters, harbour seals and Monterey cypress.

title: Tour the excess of Hearst Castle
description: 165 rooms built by William Randolph Hearst over 28 years, with a Roman pool lined in gold leaf and a zoo that once held zebras. Some still roam.

title: Stand under the tallest trees on earth in Redwood
description: Coast redwoods reach over 110m. The tallest known tree's location is deliberately unpublished to protect the ground around its roots.

title: Walk across the Golden Gate Bridge
description: 2.7km of art deco steel painted International Orange so it stays visible in fog. September and October are the clearest months.

title: Take the night tour of Alcatraz
description: A federal prison for 29 years, and occupied by Native American activists for 19 months from 1969 - graffiti from that occupation is still on the walls.

title: Ride a cable car up Hyde Street
description: The last manually operated cable car system in the world, running since 1873 by gripping a cable moving under the street at a constant 15km/h.

title: Walk among the old-growth at Muir Woods
description: One of the last uncut coast redwood stands near the coast, saved in 1908. Parking and shuttle must be reserved in advance - no walk-ups.

title: Taste Cabernet in the Napa Valley
description: The 1976 Judgement of Paris, where Napa beat Bordeaux blind, remade the region. Most tastings now need a booking.

title: See the city from Griffith Observatory
description: Free since it opened in 1935, with the Hollywood sign on one side and the whole basin on the other. Go at dusk and stay for the telescope.

title: Walk the Venice Beach boardwalk
description: Built in 1905 as a Californian imitation of Venice, canals included. Now street performers, Muscle Beach and a skate park on the sand.

title: See the tar pits at La Brea
description: Asphalt still seeping in the middle of Los Angeles, having trapped and preserved Ice Age animals for 50,000 years. Excavation continues on site.

title: Kayak the sea caves at La Jolla
description: Seven caves cut into the sandstone cliff, in a marine reserve with leopard sharks in the shallows through summer and sea lions on the rocks.

title: Spend a day in Balboa Park
description: 490 hectares of Spanish Colonial Revival buildings from the 1915 exposition, holding 17 museums and the San Diego Zoo.

title: Swim in Lake Tahoe
description: 501m deep and clear enough to see 20m down, straddling the California and Nevada line. Cold enough that most people manage about four minutes.

title: Look into Crater Lake
description: The deepest lake in the US at 594m, filling a caldera left when Mount Mazama collapsed about 7,700 years ago. Fed only by rain and snow.

title: Walk up to Multnomah Falls
description: 189m in two drops with a 1914 footbridge across the middle. Timed-entry permits apply in summer - book before you drive out.

title: Watch the tide come in at Haystack Rock
description: A 72m sea stack with tufted puffins nesting on it in spring and tide pools at its base. Oregon beaches are public and dog friendly by law.

title: Watch the sea drain into Thor's Well
description: A collapsed sea cave that appears to swallow the ocean. Best an hour either side of high tide - and people have been swept off these rocks.

title: See the Painted Hills change colour
description: Banded claystone recording 35 million years of climate change, and the colours genuinely shift with moisture and light through the day.

title: Climb Misery Ridge at Smith Rock
description: The birthplace of American sport climbing, on welded tuff above a river bend. The ridge trail is short, steep and named accurately.

title: Get lost in Powell's City of Books
description: A city block of new and used books shelved side by side - around a million of them, and the largest independent bookshop in the world.

title: Walk the Hoh Rain Forest in Olympic
description: A temperate rainforest getting up to 4 metres of rain a year, with moss hanging off every branch - and glaciers and coast in the same park.

title: Walk through Hole-in-the-Wall at Rialto Beach
description: Driftwood logs the size of telegraph poles, sea stacks in the mist, and an arch you can only reach at low tide. Check the tide table, seriously.

title: See the wildflowers at Paradise on Mount Rainier
description: An active volcano carrying more glacial ice than the rest of the lower 48 combined, with a six-week meadow bloom at its foot.

title: Watch the fish throwers at Pike Place Market
description: Trading since 1907, and one of the oldest continuously operating farmers markets in the country. The first Starbucks is across the street.

title: Look for resident orcas in the San Juan Islands
description: The Southern Resident orcas are down to about 73 animals and no longer reliably here - transient Bigg's killer whales are now the more likely sighting.

title: Stand above Palouse Falls
description: A 60m fall into a basalt bowl carved by the Missoula floods at the end of the last ice age. Best in spring melt, and the cliff edges are unfenced.

title: Take the bus into Denali
description: One 148km road into six million acres, and private vehicles are barred beyond mile 15. Grizzly, caribou, moose and wolf all along it.

title: Chase the northern lights from Fairbanks
description: Sitting under the auroral oval, with displays on roughly four nights in five when skies are clear between September and March.

title: Watch tidewater glaciers calve in Kenai Fjords
description: Nearly 40 glaciers flow off the Harding Icefield, several straight into the sea - the boat cuts its engines and you listen to the ice crack.

title: Watch bears fish at Brooks Falls
description: Brown bears catching salmon mid-air from a viewing platform in Katmai. Reachable only by float plane, and the subject of Fat Bear Week.

title: Cruise into Glacier Bay
description: Entirely covered by ice in 1794 and now open water for 100km - one of the fastest documented glacial retreats anywhere. Huna Tlingit homeland.

title: Drive the Dalton Highway to the Arctic Circle
description: 666km of mostly gravel built to service the oil pipeline, with three fuel stops on the entire route and no mobile coverage.

title: Ride the Alaska Railroad to Seward
description: Four hours from Anchorage through country with no road access at all, and one of the last railways anywhere you can flag down from the trackside.

title: Watch Kilauea glow after dark
description: One of the most active volcanoes on earth. Whether there is anything to see depends entirely on the current eruption - check the USGS status first.

title: Stargaze from Mauna Kea
description: 4,207m and the best-placed observatory site on earth. It is also sacred to Native Hawaiians, and telescope construction here remains contested.

title: Walk down to Papakolea green sand beach
description: One of only a handful of green sand beaches in the world, coloured by olivine from an eroding cinder cone. A hot 8km round trip on foot.

title: Watch sunrise from the Haleakala summit
description: 3,055m above the clouds, and about 3C at dawn. Sunrise entry needs a reservation booked up to 60 days ahead - there is no walk-up option.

title: Drive the Road to Hana
description: 620 curves and 59 one-lane bridges in 84km. Locals still use this road daily - pull over and let them past.

title: Snorkel the Molokini crater
description: A sunken volcanic crescent forming a sheltered crater with 45m visibility, and a marine reserve since 1977.

title: See the Na Pali Coast from the water
description: 27km of 1,200m cliffs with no road access at all. Boat, helicopter, or the Kalalau Trail - and that trail needs a permit and a head for heights.

title: Look into Waimea Canyon
description: Mark Twain reputedly called it the Grand Canyon of the Pacific - 16km long and 900m deep, cut into red volcanic rock.

title: Stand above the USS Arizona at Pearl Harbor
description: 1,177 crew died on the Arizona and most remain aboard. Oil still seeps from the wreck, a couple of drops a minute, eighty years on.

title: Learn to surf at Waikiki
description: Long, slow, forgiving waves and the beach where Duke Kahanamoku introduced surfing to the wider world. The gentlest place anywhere to start.

title: Walk the Strip after dark in Las Vegas
description: 6.8km of casinos built on a desert crossroads. Whatever you think of it, there is nowhere else quite like it, and walking it takes longer than it looks.

title: Find the petroglyphs at Valley of Fire
description: Nevada's oldest state park - Aztec sandstone in violent reds, with 3,000-year-old rock art at Atlatl Rock and the Fire Wave a short walk in.

title: See the Milky Way from Great Basin National Park
description: Some of the darkest skies left in the continental US, plus bristlecone pines that were already thousands of years old when Rome fell.

title: Drive the Extraterrestrial Highway
description: 158km of State Route 375 past the back gate of Area 51, with one small town, one bar and no fuel for long stretches.
